lines: My father marked it and his mother marked it, and I have marked it since I was nine.
Sixty-one years of the water coming up. Then three years of it doing nothing at all.
Somebody from the survey copied the whole chart out and asked me to stop marking it.
One mark a year, on the post, on the first spring tide. That is the whole job.
It is not a job. Nobody pays me. Somebody has to know what the water is doing.
When I am older I do the marks. Dad says it is the most boring job in Caelora.
It is not, though. It is the only one where you find out something nobody else knows.
